summary: Enhance your expertise in remote sensing with our land use and land cover mapping course. Learn from experts and apply your knowledge in real-world scenarios.
lede: Remote sensing uses satellite and airborne imagery to classify and monitor land use and land cover. For GIS analysts, remote-sensing specialists, and environmental planners, the course covers imagery preparation, training-sample design, supervised classification, and validation with confusion matrices, along with change detection and metadata to support clear map reporting.
audienceIntro: This course suits geospatial professionals who already work with maps, raster data, or environmental information and need stronger remote sensing production and validation skills.
audience: Urban and Regional Planners using change maps
modules: Earth Observation Foundations and Mapping Design
prerequisites: You should have working knowledge of GIS concepts, map projections, vector and raster data, and basic spatial analysis. Familiarity with satellite imagery is helpful but not mandatory. No programming is required for completion, although basic Python or JavaScript knowledge can support optional Google Earth Engine exploration. Advanced deep learning and object-based image analysis are taught at conceptual and operational application levels rather than production engineering depth. Bring a laptop with QGIS installed if possible; browser-based access will support selected Google Earth Engine activities.
